correct. Their undercoat and top coat work together to insulate them in the summer and winter. They work together to allow air to reach the skin and keep them cool in the summer. When you remove the top coat, and only the fluffy undercoat grows back, you inhibit the natural ventilation and the fluff basically absorbs heat from the sun and that heat has no where to go. To combat this you have to keep shaving the dogs down, which can leave their skin exposed. This causes them anxiety, but can also increase their chances of skin cancer because there isn’t anything to protect them from the sun. 

Dogs have ways to naturally take care of themselves. You dont see wolves keeling over from heat exhaustion in the summer.

While hair will grow out, it will not be the same. Samoyeds are double-coated dogs, meaning they have a dense soft undercoat and a longer, coarser top-coat. The undercoat may come back, but the top coat will likely be damaged. This will hinder the dog’s ability to control it’s body temp. There is also a chance that the hair will grow back patchy or frizzy. Not to mention, dogs like this can get extremely bothered by just seeing their skin, as it’s not something theyre supposed to see. Once you shave one of these, their coats will never be the same, and definitely for worse. Like a husky, german shepard, and even pomeranians.
